name: Kramsach
kurzbeschreibung: Municipality by Brandenberger See and Reintalersee – an Eldorado for bathers and nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kramsach is a versatile municipality in the Tyrolean Unterinntal in the Kufstein district, situated at an altitude of 520 metres where the Brandenberger Ache flows into the Inn River. Home to approximately 5,040 residents, the village nestles against the sunny southern slopes of the Rofan mountain range. Widely celebrated as the "Lake Village of Tyrol", Kramsach features an enchanting group of lakes nestled in a post-glacial moraine landscape, including Lake Reintal, Lake Krumm, Lake Frauensee, and picturesque Lake Berglstein. Combining refreshing swimming and dramatic alpine gorges with living artisanal crafts, Kramsach is home to Austria's glassmaking school, Tyrol's largest open-air agricultural museum, and the world-famous "Cemetery Museum of Cheerful Epitaphs".

History

Archaeological evidence confirms human settlement in the area as far back as the Urnfield culture around 1200 BC. The settlement was first documented between 1088 and 1097 under the name Chranzesache. For centuries, forestry and log driving along the rushing Brandenberger Ache sustained the community. In 1626, master glassmaker Wolfgang Schmid founded the Kramsach glassworks, establishing a heritage of glass refining that led to the foundation of the specialized Kramsach Glass School in 1948. In 1965, local artisan Hans Guggenberger opened the world-renowned Cemetery Museum featuring comical and witty historical burial crosses. In 1974, the Museum of Tyrolean Farmsteads opened its doors, preserving authentic historic rural architecture from valleys across Tyrol.

Getting There

Kramsach enjoys prime accessibility within the Lower Inn Valley. Motorists arrive directly via the A12 Inntal Autobahn using the Kramsach/Alpbachtal exit, or travel along the B171 federal road. Rail passengers travel along the Unterinntal mainline to the nearby Brixlegg railway station, which is served regularly by regional trains and Tyrolean S-Bahn suburban trains (line S4). From the Brixlegg station forecourt, frequent regional buses connect in minutes to Kramsach's village centre, the bathing lakes, and the open-air museums.

Tips

A visit to the Museum of Tyrolean Farmsteads offers a captivating journey into agricultural history, showcasing 14 authentic farmhouses and 37 historic outbuildings relocated from across Tyrol. The open-air Cemetery Museum provides an amusing cultural experience with its collection of wrought-iron crosses bearing humorous and philosophical epitaphs. On warm summer days, Lake Reintal beckons with swimming lawns, boat rentals, and pleasant walking circuits. Outdoor adventurers should explore the thrilling Tiefenbachklamm or Kaiserklamm gorges along the Brandenberger Ache, where turquoise waters surge through sheer limestone rock faces.
